title: Traffic orchestration policy for LTS phased promotions and safety playbooks
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: LTS channel promotions currently require a mix of manual traffic adjustments, ad-hoc canaries, and one-off rollback heuristics. This leads to uneven guardrails across teams, slow promotions, and occasional regressions that affect latency and quality.

Goal: Build a Traffic Orchestration Policy (TOP) and accompanying safety playbooks that let release engineers and SREs declare phased promotions for LTS releases with: weighted cohort routing, temporal guardrails, automated evaluation gates, simulated rehearsals (dry-run), and an auto-rollback scorer driven by SLO and quality regressions. The policy should be reusable across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments and integrate with existing feature-flagging and routing layers.

Core features and design notes:
- Declarative ramp plans: JSON/YAML policy that specifies cohorts (internal, beta customers, region A/B), percent ramps (0.5%, 5%, 25%, 50%, 100%), per-step wait windows, roll-forward and roll-back windows, and maximum allowable change per hour.
- Weighted cohorts + sticky routing: cohort weights are enforced at the router layer; sticky session keys preserved. Policies support both percentage-based and count-based cohorts for low-traffic tenants.
- Safety gates: metric-driven gates (error-rate, p95 latency, CPU/GPU saturation, quality-eval delta) and time-based gates (business hours, maintenance windows). Each gate can be soft (warn) or hard (block/rollback).
- Auto-rollback scorer: synthesizes multi-signal evidence into a single rollback score using a simple weighted model (configurable weights) and hysteresis to avoid flapping. Inputs: delta in error-rate, relative p95 increase, quality-eval regression (prompt set score), cost spike, and manual incident annotations.
- Dry-run/simulation mode: ability to run a policy against historical telemetry for a rehearsal; produces a timeline with predicted gate decisions and rollback likelihood. Simulation engine can run on production metrics snapshots for post-mortem validation.
- Release console UX: per-policy timeline, current step, projected next step, signals driving the gate decisions, and one-click manual override with audit log entry.
- Integrations: rollout controller (existing), console, alerting (PagerDuty), telemetry (Prometheus/Datadog), and prompt-set quality evals (Optimize).

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Policy schema + controller plumbing (2 weeks): define schema, controller APIs, gating primitives, and a minimal evaluation loop.
2) Router enforcement + sticky routing support (1 week): extend edge router to accept policy weights and cohort membership.
3) Auto-rollback scorer + simulation harness (2 weeks): implement scoring and the dry-run against historical windows.
4) Console UI + audit logs (1 week): show policy state, decisions, and provide manual overrides.
5) Staged rollout & rehearsals (ongoing): run internal rehearsals, then select customers, then broad LTS promotions.

Telemetry & success signals:
- Primary safety metrics: 5xx rate, p95 generation latency, CPU/GPU utilization, prompt-set pass-rate (quality score).
- SLO triggers: if 5xx increases > 0.5 percentage points sustained for 5 minutes or p95 latency increases > 30% relative to baseline for two consecutive windows, gate fails. Quality-eval drop > 3% (configurable) is a hard gate for LTS promotions.

Acceptance criteria:
- TOP controller accepts and validates the policy schema and can execute a 4-step ramp plan in staging with simulated metrics.
- Router correctly honors cohort weights and preserves sticky hashing across 3 simulated restarts.
- Auto-rollback scorer produces consistent scores in simulation and flags a rollback for at least 2 known historical incidents used in rehearsal.
- Console surfaces gate state, shows contributing signals, and records audit entries for manual overrides.
- Playbook added to runbooks with clear steps for manual rollback, escalation, and post-mortem.

Risks & trade-offs:
- False positives from noisy metrics could trigger unnecessary rollbacks; mitigation: hysteresis, multiple-window confirmation, and tuned weights.
- Added complexity in rollout pipeline; aim to keep schema opinionated and provide sane defaults.
- Cross-region differences may require region-specific baselines; initial rollout will adopt per-region baselines.

Deliverables:
- TOP schema docs and examples (confluence link below).
- Controller implementation and tests (internal repo PR).
- Simulation harness and a report showing rehearsal outcomes for 3 past incidents.
- Console UI for policy management and live state inspection.

Next steps:
- Complete initial controller PR and schedule a staging rehearsal with the SRE team (target: 2025-11-10).
- Run 2 simulated rehearsals using historical telemetry and produce a results summary.
- Iterate on thresholds and weights based on rehearsal feedback and ship a beta to the release engineering team.
acceptance_criteria: Controller accepts policy schema and simulates a 4-step ramp plan in staging
Router enforces cohort weights and preserves stickiness across restarts
Rollback scorer flags historical incidents in dry-run mode
Console displays gate state, signals, and records audit logs
Runbook for manual rollback and escalation documented
updates: 2025-10-16: Kickoff meeting with SRE and Console PM; agreed on initial schema and primary signals (5xx, p95, quality-eval).
2025-10-20: Schema v0 drafted; shared for review in #release-engineering. Feedback: add per-cohort baseline and support for low-traffic count-based cohorts.
2025-10-24: Implemented controller skeleton and unit tests; router team confirmed support for weighted cohort API (prototype PR: github.com/redwood/release-controller/pull/328).
2025-10-29: Simulation harness initial run against May-Aug 2025 telemetry; two incidents correctly produce rollback scores above threshold; shared results with SRE for tuning.
2025-11-01: Design review with Security and Compliance; no additional controls required for policy metadata; audit logging requirement accepted.
2025-11-02: Began Console integration work; UX wireframes uploaded to Confluence and linked below.
notes: Decided to start with a simple weighted scoring model for rollback rather than a full Bayesian model to reduce development time and make thresholds auditable.
We will wire the initial quality-eval signal to Optimize's prompt-set runner and treat it as a first-class hard gate for LTS promotions.
Manual override requires 2 approvers from Release Engineering + SRE; audit entry mandatory.
